title: Why do some eggs have two yolks?

seo.title: Why do some eggs have two yolks?
seo.meta_description: A double-yolk egg usually forms when a hen releases two yolks close together and both travel through the oviduct inside the same white and shell. It is especially common in young hens.
seo.search_intent: Understand how double-yolk eggs form, whether they are normal, and whether they are safe to eat.

excerpt: A double-yolk egg is usually the result of two yolks being released so close together that they travel through the oviduct at the same time and end up inside one shell. It is seen especially often in young hens whose laying cycles are still becoming synchronized.
content_html:
Crack an egg and finding two intact yolks can look like a manufacturing mistake. It is really a timing event inside the hen: two follicles can ovulate in close succession and enter the oviduct together, where they receive albumen, membranes, and one shell around them.

Why young hens produce them more often

Early in a hen's laying life, the reproductive cycle can be less synchronized. University of Nebraska–Lincoln notes that double yolks often come from young hens whose egg-production cycles have not yet settled. A classic Maine Agricultural Experiment Station study found that about 20% of pullets that began laying before seven months of age produced one or more double-yolk eggs among their early eggs, while nearly 80% of the birds never laid one.

That does not mean a young hen will keep making double yolks. They are an occasional consequence of two closely timed ovulations, and the tendency generally becomes less noticeable as laying becomes regular.

Does two yolks mean something is wrong with the egg?

No. A double yolk is a formation variation, not a spoilage sign. The usual egg-safety questions still matter: an intact shell, proper refrigeration in the U.S., clean handling, and adequate cooking when the dish calls for it.

Double-yolk eggs are often large because the shell has to contain extra yolk. But shell size cannot identify them with certainty. A large egg may still have one yolk, and the sure answer comes only after cracking the egg or candling it.

Can a double-yolk egg hatch twins?

Two fertilized yolks can theoretically begin developing, but two embryos have very little room to orient and grow normally inside one shell. Extension poultry guidance describes successful twin hatching as exceptionally rare.

What it changes in the kitchen

For frying or scrambling, nothing special is required beyond normal safe handling and cooking. For baking or custards, however, the yolk-to-white ratio is different from that of a standard single-yolk egg. In a formula where egg weight and composition matter, weighing the egg contents is more reliable than simply counting shells.

faq.question: Are double-yolk eggs safe to eat?
faq.answer: Yes. Two yolks are a formation variation and are not, by themselves, a sign of spoilage or a safety problem.

faq.question: Why are double yolks common in young hens?
faq.answer: Their laying cycles can still be irregular, making it easier for two yolks to be released in close succession.

faq.question: Can a double-yolk egg produce twin chicks?
faq.answer: It is extremely rare because two embryos have insufficient room and unfavorable conditions for normal development inside one shell.
